method_selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 and then declines from 0.601838 to 0.600686, indicating overfit. With 11 iterations left and a +0.002 convergence threshold, the highest-value available move is the complete proven capacity-plus-regularization package rather than another small atom. A wide two-stage random search over learning rate, weight decay, dropout, recency half-life, capacity, and half-epoch checkpoints can capture the known interactions among DCN-lite, BPR hybrid loss, strong regularization, and temporal recency weighting. Its measured package-level result around 0.6047 implies an honest expected gain of about +0.0029 over the 0.6018 parent, enough to clear epsilon, while avoiding repetition of the previously rejected fixed regularization dose.

rejected.reason: Also eligible and interaction-aware, but it spends substantial search budget re-establishing weak atomic stage choices; the literature package has stronger benchmark evidence and higher immediate expected value.
Its precondition is not met because there is not yet an accepted tuned-package parent in this run.
Premature closing move; the current parent is only the baseline, and ensembling should follow single-model package optimization.
A clean overfit test but expected gain is at most about +0.003 and likely near the noise floor; it is also marked running-elsewhere and has lower expected value than the full package.

expected_delta_basis: The method card reports that tuned package dials reach about 0.6047 while the node_000 parent reaches 0.6018, and identifies the sweep as necessary because untuned settings fall to 0.595-0.602.
